newsitem.title: CHINA: SHANGHAI COPPER FUTURES END UP ON LME GAINS.
newsitem.headline: SHANGHAI COPPER FUTURES END UP ON LME GAINS.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up across the board on greatly expanded volume on Friday after overnight gains on the London Metal Exhange (LME), traders said.
LME copper broke above resistance at $2,320, sparking some short-covering before it closed off peaks at $2,333, up $35.
London analysts saw the red metal settling back slightly on Friday, although the market seemed to have established itself above $2,300/10.
In Shanghai, the benchmark November 1997 contract ended at 21,360 yuan ($2,577) per tonne, up 160 yuan. It opened at 21,350 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 21,370 and a low of 21,300.
August rose 70 yuan to 20,720, September 110 to 20,910, October 100 to 21,200, December 180 to 21,400 and the January 1997 contract 200 to 21,400 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 37,910 tonnes from 17,720 tonnes.
Copper opened up and moved at high levels for most of the session.
Traders said the LME gains had boosted the confidence of long position holders in Shanghai and hot, or speculative, money continued to pour into the copper market.
"The hot money is optimistic about the later market trend in Shanghai with the help of the LME gains," one trader said.
"The good performance of aluminium late in the session also encouraged buying interest in copper," he added.
Physical copper prices in Shanghai were around 20,900 yuan per tonne, up from 28,000 yuan on Thursday due to gains on the futures market.
Traders said copper was likely to rise further early next week on improved sentiment.
Aluminium ended sharply up in active trading with significant amounts of hot money pouring into the market after the strong movements on the LME on Thursday.

LME three months aluminium snapped to $1,775 per tonne, the highest since October 9, 1995. At Thursday's peak, prices had gained $213 or nearly 14 percent in the past three weeks, fuelled by bank and fund buying. It ended up $21 at $1,762.50.
London analysts saw the market overbought and said that if aluminium closed on Fiday below $1,753/55, support would be tested at $1,720 per tonne.
In Shanghai, August aluminium rose 210 to 14,460 yuan per tonne, September 270 to 14,750, October 330 to 15,000, November 350 to 15,100 and December 390 to 15,110 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 11,820 tonnes from 5,510 tonnes.
"Most investors expect aluminium to begin a bullish run later this year, and that is what led to the sharp rises today," one trader said.
-- Shanghai Newsroom (8621) 6279-7004
